title: Okra, frozen, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Okra (Abelmoschus esculentus) is an edible pod widely used in African, Asian, and American cuisines. The frozen version is quickly steamed and packaged without added fat, preserving most nutrients and its characteristic tender flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Okra is also known as "lady's finger", "gumbo" and "bush okra".
Its mucilaginous content helps regulate blood sugar levels.
In the United States okra is a key ingredient in gumbo, while in India it is common in curries.
Freezing retains up to 90 % of vitamin C, which is often lost in fresh pods during storage.
Okra is rich in antioxidants such as quercetin and kaempferol.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low calorie content
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 20 kcal, making it an excellent choice for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Contains vitamin C and vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity, while vitamin K is essential for blood clotting.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Okra provides magnesium, potassium and iron, important for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Supports blood‑sugar control
items.content: The mucilage slows glucose absorption, helping to stabilize glycemia.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to okra.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Okra contains oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

items.title: Texture issues if overcooked
items.content: Overheating can make the pods overly soft and slimy, which may be undesirable for some.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Thaw the pods in the refrigerator or under running water, then quickly sauté, add to soups, stews, salads, or use as a side dish. It can also be blended into smoothies for extra nutrition.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen okra in its original packaging at –18 °C. After thawing, use within 2–3 days and store in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
